study: Simmons et al. 2011, Early Reading Intervention (ERI) vs typical-practice intervention
eval_evidence: ERI is a commercial program co-authored by D. C. Simmons (with Kame'enui); Simmons is first author of this evaluation, conducted under the developers' IES Early Reading Intervention project.
developer_evidence: School-based interventionists (classroom teachers, reading specialists, and trained paraprofessionals) delivered ERI; the research team provided them a modest 2-day PD rather than delivering the intervention itself.
cascade_evidence: The research team trained the interventionists directly via a 2-day PD; no train-the-trainer cascade (researchers trained the people who delivered to students).
counterfactual_evidence: Control = TPI (typical practice intervention), an active school-designed supplemental small-group reading intervention matched on time (30 min/day) and group size; some TPI groups used commercial code-based programs. Authors stress it is NOT a no-treatment/BAU control.
coaching_evidence: ERI interventionists received only a 2-day training; TPI interventionists received no study PD. Fidelity was observed/coded but no ongoing in-class coaching of interventionists is reported.
student_dose_evidence: Supplemental Tier-2 small-group pull-out intervention (groups of 3-5, 30 min/day, ~100 sessions, delivered outside the regular classroom) — a direct student-facing dose beyond regular instruction.
maturity_evidence: Single kindergarten-year supplemental program (~100 sessions over one year); no multi-year rollout or maturity axis.
